examples: 겨울인데 보일러가 안 돼서 너무 추워요.
It's winter and the boiler isn't working, so it's freezing.
calling the landlord
집주인한테 보일러 고쳐 달라고 연락했어요.
I contacted the landlord to ask them to fix the boiler.
tenant request
외출할 때는 보일러를 외출 모드로 해요.
When I go out, I set the boiler to away mode.
saving gas
nuance: 보일러 heats both the floor (온돌) and hot water in most Korean homes, so when it breaks you lose heating and hot water at once. Tenants usually report a broken 보일러 to the 집주인 or 관리사무소 right away; 'away mode' (외출 모드) is a real button people use to save gas.
mistakes: Do not confuse 보일러 (the whole heating unit) with 난방 (the heating itself).
Avoid saying 보일러가 죽었어요; the natural phrasing is 보일러가 고장 났어요 or 안 돼요.

usage: The ceiling got wet because of the leak.
It's a leak from the upstairs unit.
examples: 천장에서 물이 떨어져서 누수인 것 같아요.
Water is dripping from the ceiling, so I think it's a leak.
first noticing
누수가 윗집 때문인지 확인해야 해요.
I need to check whether the leak is from the upstairs unit.
finding fault
관리사무소에 누수 신고를 했어요.
I reported the leak to the management office.
official report
nuance: 누수 is the formal word you use when reporting water damage to a 관리사무소, landlord, or repair technician; in casual speech people also just say 물이 새요 (water is leaking). Figuring out responsibility (윗집 vs. building pipes) matters because it decides who pays for repairs.
mistakes: Do not confuse 누수 (water leak) with 누전 (electrical leakage/short).
누수 is a noun; to say it leaks, use 물이 새요, not 누수해요.

usage: There's a lot of mold on the wall.
examples: 환기를 안 하면 벽에 곰팡이가 피어요.
If you don't ventilate, mold grows on the wall.
cause and effect
장마철에는 욕실에 곰팡이가 잘 생겨요.
During the rainy season, mold easily forms in the bathroom.
seasonal problem
곰팡이 때문에 벽지를 새로 했어요.
Because of the mold, I redid the wallpaper.
consequence
nuance: 곰팡이 is a constant battle in Korean homes, especially in humid bathrooms, behind furniture against exterior walls, and during 장마 (the rainy season). The idiomatic verb is 곰팡이가 피다 (mold 'blooms') — present 피어요, past 폈어요; note 펴다 ('to unfold') is a different verb, so the mold verb is 피다, not 펴다. Bad mold is often grounds to ask a landlord for repairs.
mistakes: Do not confuse 곰팡이 (mold) with 먼지 (dust).
Native speakers say 곰팡이가 폈어요, not 곰팡이가 자랐어요, for everyday mold.

examples: 요리한 후에는 꼭 환기를 해요.
After cooking, I always air out the place.
removing smells
곰팡이가 생기지 않게 매일 환기시켜요.
I air it out daily so mold doesn't form.
preventing mold
이 방은 창문이 작아서 환기가 잘 안 돼요.
This room has a small window, so it doesn't ventilate well.
describing a flaw
nuance: 환기 (literally 'changing the air') is a daily habit Koreans take seriously, since tight, well-insulated apartments trap cooking smells and moisture that cause 곰팡이. You'll hear both 환기하다 and 환기시키다; both mean to open windows and air the place out.
mistakes: Do not confuse 환기 (ventilation) with 난방 (heating) or 냉방 (cooling).
환기 is a noun; pair it with 하다/시키다, not by adding random verbs.

usage: The water bill came out high.
I save on the water bill.
examples: 이번 달 수도세가 평소보다 많이 나왔어요.
This month's water bill came out higher than usual.
noticing a spike
월세에 수도세가 포함되어 있어요?
Is the water bill included in the monthly rent?
key question when renting
누수 때문에 수도세 폭탄을 맞았어요.
I got hit with a huge water bill because of a leak.
수도세 폭탄 = bill shock
nuance: 수도세 (also 수도 요금) is one of the 공과금 (utility bills) tenants juggle. A crucial question before signing a lease is whether it's 포함 (included) in the rent; the slang 요금 폭탄 ('bill bomb') describes a shockingly high bill, often from a hidden 누수.
mistakes: Do not confuse 수도세 (water bill) with 수돗물 (tap water).
Use 수도세가 나왔어요 / 수도세를 내요; do not say 수도세를 사다.

usage: The electricity bill is scary in summer.
examples: 에어컨을 많이 틀어서 전기세가 무서워요.
I ran the AC a lot, so I'm scared of the electricity bill.
summer worry
전기세 아끼려고 안 쓰는 콘센트는 다 뽑아요.
To save on electricity, I unplug all the outlets I'm not using.
saving habit
전기세가 지난달보다 두 배나 나왔어요.
The electricity bill came out double last month's.
comparing with 보다
nuance: 전기세 (formally 전기 요금) follows a progressive rate (누진제), so heavy summer AC use can spike the bill dramatically; '전기세 폭탄' is a common summer complaint. Strictly 요금 is more correct than 세 (which means 'tax'), but everyone says 전기세 in daily life.
mistakes: Do not confuse 전기세 (electricity bill) with 전기 (electricity itself).
Although it ends in 세 (tax), it is a usage fee; the textbook term is 전기 요금.

usage: The gas bill is high in winter.
The gas bill is a burden.
I try to save on the gas bill.
examples: 겨울에 보일러를 많이 틀어서 가스비가 많이 나왔어요.
I ran the boiler a lot in winter, so the gas bill was high.
boiler and gas link
가스비 아끼려고 보일러를 외출 모드로 해 놔요.
To save on gas, I keep the boiler on away mode.
money-saving tip
이번 겨울은 가스비가 작년보다 더 비싸요.
This winter the gas bill is more expensive than last year.
comparing years
nuance: 가스비 (formally 도시가스 요금) spikes in winter because the 보일러 runs on gas for both heating and hot water. News about rising 가스비 is a recurring topic, and tenants often link a high 가스비 directly to how much they used the 보일러.
mistakes: Do not confuse 가스비 (gas bill) with 가스레인지 (gas stove).
Avoid 가스비를 사다; bills are 내다 (pay) or 나오다 (come out).

examples: 이사 오기 전에 도배를 새로 했어요.
Before moving in, I had it freshly wallpapered.
move-in renovation
곰팡이 때문에 도배를 다시 해야 해요.
Because of mold, I have to redo the wallpaper.
mold consequence
집주인이 도배랑 장판을 새로 해 줬어요.
The landlord redid the wallpaper and flooring for me.
landlord upgrade
nuance: 도배 (papering the walls) and 장판 (the vinyl floor) are the two things Koreans almost always refresh when moving into or renting out a place; they're often mentioned as a pair. A tenant may negotiate for the landlord to redo 도배 before moving in, especially if there's old or stained 벽지.
mistakes: Do not confuse 도배 (the act of wallpapering) with 벽지 (the wallpaper material itself).
도배 needs 하다 to be a verb; do not treat it as a standalone action word.

examples: 보일러를 켜면 장판이 따뜻해져요.
When I turn on the boiler, the floor covering gets warm.
ondol floor
오래된 장판이 누래서 새로 깔았어요.
The old flooring was yellowed, so I laid new one.
replacing
누수 때문에 장판 밑이 다 젖었어요.
Because of the leak, under the flooring got all wet.
water damage
nuance: 장판 is the smooth vinyl sheet laid over the heated 온돌 floor in most Korean homes; the verb that goes with it is 깔다 (to lay/spread). Together with 도배, it's a standard checklist item when assessing or renovating a rental, and damaged 장판 (lifted, yellowed, water-stained) is a common point of negotiation.
mistakes: Do not confuse 장판 (the vinyl floor sheet) with 바닥 (the floor itself).
Use 장판을 깔다 (lay) not 장판을 입다 or other random verbs.

usage: I plug it into the outlet.
I unplug it from the outlet.
examples: 휴대폰 충전기를 콘센트에 꽂았어요.
I plugged the phone charger into the outlet.
everyday action
이 방은 콘센트가 하나밖에 없어요.
This room has only one outlet.
describing a flaw
외출할 때 안 쓰는 콘센트는 뽑아요.
When going out, I unplug outlets I'm not using.
saving electricity
nuance: 콘센트 (a Japanese-origin loanword, not 'consent') is the wall socket; the plug itself is 플러그 and the verbs are 꽂다 (plug in) and 뽑다 (unplug). The number of 콘센트 is a real concern in older or small rooms, and unplugging unused ones is a common 전기세-saving habit.
mistakes: Do not assume 콘센트 means 'consent'; it means the wall outlet.
Do not confuse 콘센트 (the socket on the wall) with 플러그 (the plug on the cord).

usage: I throw out the food waste.
examples: 음식물쓰레기는 일반 쓰레기랑 따로 버려야 해요.
Food waste has to be thrown out separately from regular trash.
key rule for residents
우리 아파트는 음식물쓰레기를 카드로 버려요.
Our apartment disposes of food waste by card.
RFID smart bins
여름에는 음식물쓰레기를 빨리 버려야 냄새가 안 나요.
In summer you have to throw out food waste quickly or it smells.
practical tip
nuance: 음식물쓰레기 must be separated from 일반쓰레기 and 재활용 by law, and many apartments use weight-based RFID 음식물쓰레기 bins (you tag a card and dump it). Getting this wrong can mean a fine or an annoyed building manager, so it's a real survival skill for new residents.
mistakes: Do not confuse 음식물쓰레기 (food waste) with 일반쓰레기 (general non-recyclable trash).
Don't write the bins off as optional; mixing food waste into general trash can incur a fine (과태료).

usage: The maintenance fee came out high.
Is it included in the maintenance fee?
How much is the maintenance fee?
examples: 월세 말고도 관리비를 매달 따로 내야 해요.
Besides rent, I have to pay a maintenance fee separately every month.
renting reality
관리비에 수도세랑 청소비가 포함되어 있어요.
The maintenance fee includes the water bill and cleaning fee.
what it covers
겨울에는 난방비 때문에 관리비가 확 올라가요.
In winter the maintenance fee jumps because of heating costs.
seasonal rise
nuance: 관리비 is the monthly building-maintenance fee covering things like cleaning, security, elevator, and often part of the utilities; it's charged on top of 월세 and surprises many newcomers. Always ask what the 관리비 covers (수도세, 난방비, 인터넷 etc.) before signing, since a 'cheap' rent can hide a high 관리비.
mistakes: Do not confuse 관리비 (monthly maintenance fee) with 보증금 (the refundable deposit).
관리비 is usually separate from 월세; don't assume rent already includes it.
